questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Montenegro?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy and demographics” part of the Montenegro article.

questions.proof: The traditional old capital of Montenegro is Cetinje, but Podgorica is the new capital.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Montenegro on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Montenegro on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Podgorica?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Montenegro is Podgorica.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Montenegro?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Montenegro on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Montenegro article.

questions.proof: Inland (to the East and South-East) it also has a common border with Serbia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Montenegro?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Montenegro is the euro.
